hook: This humanoid robot learned cornhole from one AI model and one video of a person.
caption:
This humanoid robot learned cornhole from one AI model and one video of a person.

Gemini Argon watched someone throw, then took control of the Apollo robot, built its own simulation and trained its own throws.

The split screen shows the real robot next to the sim it trained in.

Would you let a robot beat you at cornhole? 👇

checked: Post text (https://x.com/normandipalo/status/2110054176382206379): Gemini Argon, Apollo humanoid, one video of a person, sim env + sysID + trained launches; credit @normandipalo.
Frames 1-8: Google DeepMind credit on the researcher (frame 1); split screen real Apollo cam vs MuJoCo sim (frame 2); UI prompt reads 'Gemini 4 Argon' (frame 5).

Web search (standard), no official Google page found: coverage of Google's Gemini 4 Argon announcement (https://interestingengineering.com/videos/googles-gemini-4-argon-taught-a-humanoid-robot-to-play-cornhole, https://cryptobriefing.com/gemini-4-argon-robot-cornhole/). Confirms the Apptronik Apollo test and seven cornhole shots in a row. Caveat: one write-up says the robot needed a few real throws before the run, so 'one video' is the creator's claim, not independently confirmed; the hook uses it as the creator's claim and the caption says 'watched a video'.
Owner revision ('This robot learned it from one model') applied to the hook; strategy directive (hook = guess prompt <= 7 words) not used because the owner's revision takes priority.
